title: From PDB to topology
story: This track follows the classic lysozyme-in-water tutorial. 1aki.pdb is hen lysozyme with its crystal waters. First save a copy without the waters (lines with HOH) as 1AKI_clean.pdb. Then build the GROMACS files with pdb2gmx: coordinates 1AKI_processed.gro and a topology, using the AMBER99SB-ILDN force field and SPC/E water.

lesson.title: pdb2gmx: describe the protein

parts.note: Reads a PDB file and writes what GROMACS needs: coordinates (.gro), a topology (topol.top) and position restraints (posre.itp).
The output coordinates, with hydrogens added.
The water model the topology will use.
The force field: the rules for how atoms push and pull on each other.

lesson.why: The topology lists every atom, its charge and its bonds. Every later step reads it.
lesson.without: Leave out `-ff` or `-water` and pdb2gmx stops to ask you to pick from a menu.

tasks.text: Run pdb2gmx to make 1AKI_processed.gro and topol.top

hints: `grep -v HOH 1aki.pdb > 1AKI_clean.pdb` keeps every line that does not contain HOH.
Look at the end of topol.top with `tail topol.top`: the [ molecules ] section lists one protein.
